newsitem.title: JAPAN: Firm makes women's underwear from plastic bottles.
newsitem.headline: Firm makes women's underwear from plastic bottles.

text.p: A Japanese lingerie maker unveiled a new line of women's underwear on Wednesday made from recycled plastic bottles.
It takes three and a half 1.5-litre plastic bottles to make a bra and a pair of panties, said Triumph International Japan Ltd, a subsidiary of Germany's Triumph International AG.
It said it had made the underwear from recycled polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles used to hold mineral water and soft drinks.
"We came up with the idea of recycling PET bottles to make lingerie, because the difficulty of recycling them had become a matter of concern in society," a Triumph spokeswoman said.
The company's new product is made entirely from soft cloth and lace produced from chemically processed fibers of crushed plastic bottles, Triumph said.
"The campaign model said our lingerie feels just like ordinary underwear," the spokeswoman said. "But she also said it would be more comfortable if it fit closer to the body."

She said the company plans to improve the material to add To enhance its nature-conscious image, the product modelled in Tokyo on Wednesday was featured in a soft green colour, with a leafy pattern used on the lace, Triumph said.
The environment-friendly underwear will be sold experimentally in Japan from this autumn for about 7,000 yen ($55) apiece, it said.
The company said there were no plans to market the new product overseas.
